subject: phase3_cumulative_context_budget
statement: Implement provider-free cumulative context and tool-call controls for all Phase 3 Codex provider positions without launching another benchmark instance.
selected_option: bind 32768-token active-context compaction with a 12-call soft warning and a 16-slot atomic PreToolUse execution boundary

alternatives.option: terminate Codex externally at the hard boundary
alternatives.rejected_reason: Killing the process can lose terminal provider usage and weakens recovery evidence.
Prompt compliance is not a deterministic execution boundary.

alternatives.option: lower only the per-tool output limit
alternatives.rejected_reason: The Requests screen shows that cumulative sampling rounds dominate even when individual tool outputs are bounded.

rationale: Retained valid provider positions completed 5 to 13 tool calls, while the failed treatment direct worker completed 41. The selected 12-call warning and 16-call hard boundary preserve headroom above every retained valid sample and reject later tools in the observed diagnostic loop. PreToolUse reserves each admitted slot under a file lock before execution, so parallel requests cannot overshoot. Codex auto-compaction bounds active history, while blocked tools do not prevent a final response or terminal usage. All controls are frozen into the protocol, launch registration, and exact Codex command.
expected_outcome: Produce a backward-compatible, provider-free tested execution boundary that can be frozen into a later scored bundle by a separate authorization.
acceptance_refs: protocol rejects partial policy fields and invalid soft-hard ordering
registered commands require exact compaction and PreToolUse configuration
hook tests prove warning, hard rejection, per-turn isolation, and locked concurrent counting
transcript replay leaves retained valid samples below the hard boundary
